To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Cryo-ecosystems on Arctic ice shelves are characterized by extremophilic heterotrophs and extremotrophic autotrophs that are adapted to the extreme conditions of the ice shelf environment.

(i) microbial mat communities on the ice shelves in the high arctic provide an extreme cryo-ecology; (ii) the mats are heterotrophic, extremotrophic and extremophilic; (iii) the extremophilic bacteria are specifically adapted to ambient ice shelf conditions; (iv) the extremotrophic response is due to a suite of pigments that absorb from the UV-B to red wavelength range.
the high arctic ice shelves are a unique habitat for extremophilic bacteria that have evolved to tolerate high irradiance, low temperature and variable salinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ecology of microbial mats that grow on the surface of Arctic ice shelves.
the physiological responses of microbial mat communities to the multiple stressors associated with a cryo-ecology.
the ecology of microbial mat communities on ice shelves and the role of pigments in their adaptation to the harsh conditions of the polar environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

extremophilic bacteria dominate the ice shelf microbial community but the extremotrophic autotrophs are also present and are likely to be more significant than the heterotrophs in the longer-term dynamics of the ice shelf ecosystem.
the heterotrophic bacterial community was extremotrophic whereas the autotrophs were extremotolerant.

the heterotrophic bacterial mat communities are extremophilic whereas the autotrophs are extremotolerant and extremotrophic, with a suite of pigments that provide a comprehensive broadband protection against the multiple stressors in this extreme cryoenvironment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microbial communities in the Arctic ice shelf are extremotrophic, with extremophilic and extremotrophic components.
the extremotrophic response of the autotrophs is due to a combination of extremophilic and extremotrophic strategies.
the heterotrophic bacterial community is extremophilic whereas the autotrophs are extremotrophic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microbial mats on Arctic ice shelves are dominated by extremotolerant extremotrophic communities.
microbial mats in the Arctic are extremotrophic and that the extremophilic heterotrophic bacteria may be more sensitive to changes in the environment than the extremotrophic autotrophic community.
the extremophilic bacteria are well adapted to this extreme cryo-ecological niche.
